samples.prompt: Write a reflective narrative about revisiting a memory from your youth involving an unfinished or newly constructed building. Describe your philosophical impressions of the empty structure at the time and include a specific incident or action you took during your visit.
samples.generated:
I went back to the <GROUP> and looked at it again. It was a thing
of a very beautiful and terrible simplicity; a simple mass of stone
and wood in the midst of a forest, like the end of a fairy-tale. It
was so new that I felt as if I had just come out of an earthquake.
And though it had only just been finished, its beauty seemed to have
been complete for ever. It was like a giant who was not quite dead. The
trees were young trees, and the grass was green; but there was no life
in them. The whole air was still and silent. There was not even a bird
to be heard in the trees. The wind did not blow in the leaves of the
trees; nor did the wind blow upon anything else in that strange place.
I walked round it slowly and quietly; and then I climbed up into the
highest point of its roof, and sat looking down upon the world. Then I
began to look about me. The world looked very small and grey. I saw
nothing but old men and old women, and boys and girls, sitting on the
grass beneath my feet. They were all old-fashioned in their appearance,
as if they had never known any change since the creation. I looked at
them, and said to myself, “This is the world.”
